newsitem.title: INDIA: India's United Front postpones oil price meeting.
newsitem.headline: India's United Front postpones oil price meeting.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's ruling United Front coalition has postponed a meeting set for Sunday to consider raising the domestic prices of some petroleum products, a spokesman said.
"It is not on (June) 15th," Information Minister Jaipal Reddy, the alliance spokesman, told Reuters by telephone on Friday. He said the coalition had not yet set a fresh date for the meeting.
D. Raja, a senior leader of the Communist Party of India (CPI), said the meeting might be held on Monday.
The 15-party United Front took up the oil price issue at a meeting on May 25 but was unable to reach a consensus.
Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram have been pressing for increases in petroleum product prices, while leftwing parties want alternatives to be considered.

At the end of March, the government owed domestic oil firms 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March. The debt, called theoil pool account deficit, represents money owed by the government to the companies for selling below market prices.

The oil subsidy bill is estimated at some 180 billion rupees. It includes the cost of products sold below market prices plus a cross-subsidisation element under which some products, like gasoline, are priced above market prices.
